Description is here https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle_kick.  is an acrobatic strike where a player kicks an airborne ball rearward in midair. It is achieved by throwing the body backward up into the air and, before descending to the ground, making a shearing movement with the lower limbs to get the ball-striking leg in front of the other. In most languages, the manoeuvre is named after either the cycling motion or the scissor motion that it resembles.

accessibility_stats_comparison_explanati.english:
The Player Traits chart highlights a player's statistical strengths and weaknesses, in comparison to similar players.

Each stat is adjusted on a per 90 basis and includes matches from the past 365 days.

Players are then compared to positional peers from similar leagues, and placed into a percentile ranking. For example, a player with a 90% percentile ranking on Chances Created means that they create more chances than 90% of players in their position in similar leagues.

Full details on comparisons can be read in our FAQ.
accessibility_stats_comparison_explanati.value:
A játékosjellemzők ábrája megmutatja egy játékos statisztikai erősségeit és gyengeségeit a hasonló játékosokhoz képest.

Minden statisztika 90 percre van vetítve, és az elmúlt 365 nap meccseit tartalmazza.

A játékosokat ezután hasonló bajnokságok azonos posztú játékosaival vetjük össze, és percentilis rangsorba soroljuk. Ha például egy játékos a kialakított helyzetekben a 90. percentilisen áll, akkor több helyzetet alakít ki, mint a hasonló bajnokságokban azonos poszton játszó játékosok 90 százaléka.

Az összevetés részleteit a GYIK-ban olvashatod.

common_deepstats_explanation.english:
All data is calculated based on stats provided by Opta.

The FotMob player rating is calculated based on more than 100 individual stats per player per match.

A match in the per match ratings is any match the participant has been involved in even if he came on as substitute in the last few minutes.

A player must have played at least 50% of all matches and at least 90 minutes (for the per 90 stats) to be included in the rankings.
common_deepstats_explanation.value:
Minden adat az Opta által szolgáltatott statisztikákon alapul.

A FotMob játékosértékelése játékosonként és meccsenként több mint 100 egyéni statisztikán alapul.

A meccsenkénti értékeléseknél minden olyan meccs beszámít, amelyen a játékos szerepelt, akkor is, ha csak az utolsó percekben állt be csereként.

A rangsorokban csak az a játékos szerepel, aki az összes meccs legalább 50 százalékán pályára lépett, és legalább 90 percet játszott (a 90 percre vetített statisztikáknál).

common_estimated_transfer_value_descript.english:
Estimated Transfer Value (ETV) is an estimate of what a player could be worth if they were sold today.

It’s calculated using historical transfer data and a range of performance and context factors, including:

• player performance and development
• age and future potential
• how often and at what level they play
• position
• team and league strength
• remaining contract length

ETV focuses on the player themselves, not rumours or which club might buy them.

The value is updated regularly to reflect changes over time.
common_estimated_transfer_value_descript.value:
A becsült átigazolási érték (ETV) azt becsüli meg, mennyit érhetne egy játékos, ha ma eladnák.

Számításához korábbi átigazolási adatokat és számos teljesítmény- és környezeti tényezőt használunk, például:

• a játékos teljesítménye és fejlődése
• életkor és jövőbeli potenciál
• milyen gyakran és milyen szinten játszik
• poszt
• a csapat és a bajnokság erőssége
• a szerződés hátralévő időtartama

Az ETV magára a játékosra összpontosít, nem a pletykákra vagy arra, melyik klub vásárolhatná meg.

Az értéket rendszeresen frissítjük, hogy kövesse az idő közbeni változásokat.

common_penalty_off_target.comment: Shown in match facts under the name of the player who took a penalty that was not scored because it went wide, over the bar, or hit the post or crossbar, and was not saved. See "missed_penalty". See "saved_penalty". Two parts separated by a hyphen: the first part is the term for a penalty that was not scored, identical in both keys; the second part says what happened to this one kick. Do not repeat the word for penalty in the second part. Phrase both parts as what happened to the kick, not as something the named player did. One single kick. Keep both parts short: this is one line on a narrow card, under the player name. Use the standard football term for a shot off target, one that also covers hitting the woodwork; not a word that means only "wide", and not one that means the ball left the field of play.

seo_bridge_timeout_message.comment: Body paragraph below bridge_timeout_title on the same full-screen error page. Tells the user the app timed out while loading their user data (account/profile data fetched on startup) and directs them to open predict.fotmob.com in a web browser as a workaround. Use "FotMob" verbatim (proper noun) — do not translate or transliterate the product name. Keep the URL "predict.fotmob.com" verbatim — do not translate, transliterate, change the domain, or wrap it in markup. For RTL locales (ar, fa, ckb), make sure punctuation falls on the correct side of the sentence and the URL stays LTR. Tone: friendly, neutral, calm. ≤ 120 chars per locale.
seo_bridge_timeout_message.english: The app timed out while loading your user data. Please go to predict.fotmob.com in a web browser.
seo_bridge_timeout_message.value: Időtúllépés történt a felhasználói adataid betöltése közben. Nyisd meg a predict.fotmob.com oldalt egy böngészőben.

seo_bridge_timeout_title.comment: Title (h1) of a full-screen error page shown when the FotMob native shell fails to handshake with the predictor web app within ~10 seconds. The page replaces the entire app UI; no header, no footer, no other text on screen. The user is inside the FotMob mobile app (iOS or Android webview) and cannot retry from this page — they must close and re-open the app. Tone: friendly, neutral, calm — a short acknowledgement of an error, not a technical phrase. No exclamation marks. ≤ 30 chars per locale.

seo_in_app_browser_open_in_chrome.comment: This is the label on a button that opens the current page in Google Chrome. It appears in the in-app browser escape card. "Chrome" is a brand name and should not be translated. Tone: short button label.

seo_in_app_browser_or_manually.comment: This is a small label/heading shown as a divider between the automatic "Open in browser" buttons and the manual app-specific instructions below. It introduces the manual instructions section with "Or manually:" — translate naturally as a transitional phrase introducing an alternative method. Tone: brief, understated.

seo_in_app_browser_sign_in_not_reliable.comment: This is explanatory body text shown below the in_app_browser_open_in_browser_title heading inside the same card. It explains why the user needs to switch browsers. The %1$s placeholder is replaced at runtime with the name of the social media app the user is in (e.g. "Instagram", "TikTok", "Facebook") — the resulting text reads like "Sign-in doesn't work reliably in Instagram's browser." Keep the %1$s placeholder exactly as-is; do not translate or modify it. "Safari" and "Chrome" are brand names and should not be translated. Tone: informative, helpful.
seo_in_app_browser_sign_in_not_reliable.english: Sign-in doesn't work reliably in %1$s's browser. Please open this page in Safari or Chrome.
seo_in_app_browser_sign_in_not_reliable.value: A bejelentkezés nem működik megbízhatóan a(z) %1$s böngészőjében. Nyisd meg ezt az oldalt Safariban vagy Chrome-ban.

seo_in_app_browser_try_anyway.comment: This is the label of a small, de-emphasized text link at the bottom of the in-app browser escape screen. It lets the user bypass the warning and attempt to sign in using OAuth directly within the in-app browser (which may fail). The parenthetical "(may not work)" is an important caveat — preserve it. Tone: understated, secondary option, with a warning.
seo_in_app_browser_try_anyway.english: Try signing in here anyway (may not work)
seo_in_app_browser_try_anyway.value: Bejelentkezés itt mégis (lehet, hogy nem működik)

seo_in_app_browser_warning_headline.comment: This is a bold headline text shown in a warning banner at the top of the sign-in screen when the app detects the user is browsing inside a social media app's built-in browser (e.g. Instagram, TikTok, Facebook). It alerts the user that logging in may not work properly. "In-app browser" is a technical term referring to the simplified web browser embedded inside social media apps — use whatever phrasing is natural and understandable in the target language to convey this concept. Tone: informative, slightly urgent but not alarming.
seo_in_app_browser_warning_headline.english: Login may not work in this in-app browser
seo_in_app_browser_warning_headline.value: Ebben az alkalmazáson belüli böngészőben a bejelentkezés lehet, hogy nem működik

seo_in_app_browser_warning_may_fail.comment: This is a warning message shown on the sign-in screen of a sports prediction app (FotMob Predict) when a user has chosen to attempt signing in despite being inside a social media app's built-in browser (e.g. Instagram, TikTok, Facebook). It appears as small yellow warning text inside a bordered card, directly above the OAuth sign-in buttons (Google, Facebook, Apple). The %1$s placeholder is replaced with the name of the social media app (e.g. "Instagram", "TikTok"). Below this text there is a separate clickable "Go back" link, so this string itself does not need to contain any link or call to action — it is purely informational, explaining why signing in might not work. The phrase "go back" in this string refers to returning to the previous screen where the user can open the page in a real browser instead. Tone: cautionary but helpful, not alarming. "Browser" here refers to a full browser like Safari or Chrome, as opposed to the limited in-app browser embedded in social media apps.
seo_in_app_browser_warning_may_fail.english: Sign-in may not work in %1$s's browser. For the best experience, go back and open this page in your browser.
seo_in_app_browser_warning_may_fail.value: A bejelentkezés lehet, hogy nem működik a(z) %1$s böngészőjében. A legjobb élményért lépj vissza, és nyisd meg ezt az oldalt a böngésződben.

Tone: polite, instructional.

seo_in_app_browser_warning_subline.value: A folytatáshoz nyisd meg ezt az oldalt a készüléked böngészőjében (Safari vagy Chrome).

seo_joincode_error_generic.comment: Fallback error message used in three places: (a) inline under the typed-code input on unexpected failures, (b) body of the full-screen "Couldn't join the league" error, and (c) the success-state toast equivalent doesn't exist — this is purely a generic error. Tone: brief, non-alarming, suggests retry.

seo_joincode_error_invalid_alphabet.comment: Inline form-validation error shown while the user is typing/pasting into the "Enter a league code" input. Appears when the input contains digits, symbols, or the specific letters I, L, O. The exclusion of I/L/O is intentional — they're omitted from the alphabet because they're visually ambiguous with 1/0. The letter names should stay as their English glyphs (I, L, O) — they refer to literal characters, not translatable words. The en-dash in "A–Z" should be preserved if your script uses Latin A–Z; if you adapt to a different script, use the equivalent range concept.

seo_joincode_error_invalid_alphabet.value: A kódok csak A–Z betűket tartalmazhatnak (az I, L és O kivételével).

seo_joincode_error_invalid_code.comment: Inline error under the "Enter a league code" input (and toast on the invite-link page) when the league code has the right shape but the backend rejects it — e.g. a typo, a code that was once valid but isn't anymore, or a code that's the wrong length. Tone: friendly, action-oriented ("try again"). The word "code" here means a short alphanumeric league invite code shown on the share card.
seo_joincode_error_invalid_code.english: This invite code isn't valid. Please check it and try again.

seo_prediction_stats_correct_outcome_ari.comment: Screen-reader label (aria-label + title tooltip) on the 'correct outcome' stats cluster shown under finished match cards. 'Correct outcome' means the user predicted the right winner OR a draw, but not necessarily the exact score (a weaker condition than 'perfect'). Visible UI shows a frost/blue gem icon + percent and count (e.g. '30% (300)'). %1$s is the localized absolute count of users (e.g. '300', '1,512'); %2$s is the already-localized percent string with its '%' sign baked in — do NOT add another percent sign. Order of placeholders MAY be changed for grammar (e.g. RTL or languages where the percent leads). Provide plural forms appropriate for the target language (CLDR rules apply — e.g. ar uses one/two/few/many/other; ja/ko/zh-Hans/th/vi/id/my use other only). Tone is neutral/informational, not promotional. See also [prediction_stats_perfect_aria] — the two strings should read in matching register, and the wording for 'correct outcome' must be semantically distinct from 'perfect' (which means the exact final score).

plurals.one: %1$s tippelő találta el a meccs kimenetelét (%2$s)
plurals.other: %1$s tippelő találta el a meccs kimenetelét (%2$s)

seo_prediction_stats_perfect_aria.comment: Screen-reader label (aria-label + title tooltip) on the 'perfect predictions' stats cluster shown under finished match cards. A 'perfect' prediction is one where the user predicted the exact final score. The visible UI shows a gold gem icon followed by the percent and count (e.g. '5% (50)') — this string is what assistive tech announces and what hover-tooltip shows, so it should read as a complete natural sentence. %1$s is the localized absolute count of users (e.g. '50', '1,512'). %2$s is the already-localized percent string with its '%' sign baked in (e.g. '5%', '0.007%', '100%') — do NOT add another percent sign. Order of placeholders MAY be changed for grammar (e.g. RTL or languages where the percent leads). 'Users' here means people who placed a prediction on this match; if your locale has a more idiomatic term like 'players' or 'predictors', prefer that. Keep the parenthesis style natural for the locale; if your locale prefers a different separator (em dash, comma) over '( )', adapt freely. Provide plural forms appropriate for the target language (CLDR rules apply — e.g. ar uses one/two/few/many/other; ja/ko/zh-Hans/th/vi/id/my use other only). Tone is neutral/informational, not promotional. See also [prediction_stats_correct_outcome_aria] — the two strings should read in matching register.

plurals.one: %1$s tippelő találta el a pontos végeredményt (%2$s)
plurals.other: %1$s tippelő találta el a pontos végeredményt (%2$s)

seo_prizes_and_contest_rules.comment: Section heading on a collapsible dropdown card in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes & contest rules dropdown (Leagues tab). Should be short (≤ ~30 chars rendered) — it sits next to a chevron. The "&" is intentional shorthand; localise to whatever your language uses for joining two nouns in a heading (e.g. "and", "und", "et", "y"). Title-case if the language conventionally title-cases headings.

seo_prizes_summary_contest_period.comment: Bullet stating the official start/end window of the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 contest. Do NOT translate the dates, times, or "ET" (Eastern Time) — these must match the Official Rules verbatim. You may translate "Contest runs from … to …" but keep the date/time tokens intact. Example (German): "Der Wettbewerb läuft vom June 11, 2026, 3:00 PM ET bis July 19, 2026, 6:00 PM ET."
seo_prizes_summary_contest_period.english: Contest runs from June 11, 2026, 3:00 PM ET to July 19, 2026, 6:00 PM ET.
seo_prizes_summary_contest_period.value: A játék időtartama: June 11, 2026, 3:00 PM ET – July 19, 2026, 6:00 PM ET.

seo_prizes_summary_free_to_enter.comment: First bullet in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. This is sweepstakes boilerplate required by US contest law — every clause must be preserved: (a) entry is free, (b) no purchase needed, (c) US residents only, (d) 18 and older. The "18+" notation can be rendered as your locale prefers ("18 ans et plus", "ab 18 Jahren", etc.). "US residents" must remain "US" — do not localise to "American" or expand to "United States of America" unless your language requires it. Do not soften the eligibility language — accuracy here is legally required.
seo_prizes_summary_free_to_enter.english: Free to enter. No purchase necessary. Open to US residents aged 18+.
seo_prizes_summary_free_to_enter.value: Ingyenes részvétel. Vásárlás nem szükséges. Csak legalább 18 éves US-lakosok vehetnek részt.

seo_prizes_summary_one_account.comment: Final eligibility bullet in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. Short. Clear. Don't elaborate ("Each participant may register only one account") unless that's how your locale would phrase such a rule.

seo_prizes_summary_ordinary_time.comment: Longest bullet in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. Two parts joined by an em-dash: (1) which match phase the prediction refers to — 90 minutes + stoppage time, not extra time, not penalty shootout; (2) practical advice — if you expect knockout extra time, pick a draw. Use the locale's football-specific terms: "stoppage time" → injury time / Nachspielzeit / temps additionnel etc.; "extra time" → the extra 30 minutes after 90 (NOT stoppage time); "penalties" → penalty shootout (not penalty kicks during regular play); "knockout match" → elimination/knockout round game. Keep the em-dash structure if your locale uses em-dashes; otherwise use a sentence break.
seo_prizes_summary_ordinary_time.english: All predictions are for the score at the end of 90 minutes (plus stoppage time). Extra time and penalties don't count — if you think a knockout match will go to extra time, predict a draw.
seo_prizes_summary_ordinary_time.value: Minden tipp a 90 perc (plusz a ráadás) utáni állásra vonatkozik. A hosszabbítás és a tizenegyespárbaj nem számít – ha szerinted egy egyenes kieséses meccs hosszabbításba megy, tippelj döntetlent.

seo_prizes_summary_predict_each_match.comment: Bullet describing the core gameplay action in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. "Result" here means the final score outcome (win/draw/loss + score). "Kickoff" is the football term for match start — use the locale's football-specific term ("coup d'envoi", "Anpfiff", etc.), not a generic "before the match starts". Preserve "World Cup" verbatim.
seo_prizes_summary_predict_each_match.english: Predict the result of each World Cup match before kickoff.
seo_prizes_summary_predict_each_match.value: Tippeld meg minden World Cup-meccs eredményét a kezdőrúgás előtt.

seo_prizes_summary_prize.comment: Bullet describing the prize in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. Two sentences: (1) explains who wins (highest-ranked US user when the tournament ends), what they win (PS5), and the approximate retail value; (2) tiebreaker rule (random draw — not e.g. "earliest score" or "most perfect predictions"). Keep "PlayStation 5" and "US$499.99" verbatim. "approx. value" is shorthand for "approximate retail value" — feel free to write it out if your locale doesn't shorten "approximate" the same way.
seo_prizes_summary_prize.english: Top of the US leaderboard at the end of the tournament wins a PlayStation 5 (approx. value US$499.99). Ties broken by random drawing.
seo_prizes_summary_prize.value: A torna végén a US-ranglista élén álló játékos egy PlayStation 5-öt nyer (becsült érték: US$499.99). Holtverseny esetén sorsolás dönt.

seo_prizes_summary_three_points_score.comment: Scoring rule bullet in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. Keep "3 points" with the numeral. "Scoreline" is the football term for the final score (e.g. 2–1). Use your locale's football-specific term — not "score" if "scoreline" has a distinct meaning in the language. The 3 points is inclusive of the 2-point outcome award (not 5 total) — but that nuance lives in the full Official Rules page, not in this summary.

seo_prizes_summary_two_points_outcome.comment: Scoring rule bullet in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes summary. Keep "2 points" with the numeral. "Correct outcome" means correctly picking who wins or that it's a draw, without needing the exact score. "Winner or draw" is the clarifying parenthetical — render the parenthetical as your locale standardly formats parenthetical lists.
seo_prizes_summary_two_points_outcome.english: 2 points for the correct outcome (winner or draw).
seo_prizes_summary_two_points_outcome.value: 2 pont a helyes kimenetelért (győztes vagy döntetlen).

seo_prizes_view_official_rules.comment: Link CTA in the FotMob Predict World Cup 2026 prizes dropdown that opens the full legal rules page. "Official Rules" is the formal/legal name of the document; in some languages legal documents are conventionally capitalised — follow that convention.

seo_sign_in_error_message.comment: Body paragraph below the title on the same error page. Also used as the toast message shown when a failed sign-in is detected inside a native app webview. Intentionally generic — we do not surface the underlying error code to the user. Tone: matter-of-fact, reassuring, not blaming the user.
seo_sign_in_error_message.english: Something went wrong while signing in. Please try again.
seo_sign_in_error_message.value: Hiba történt a bejelentkezés során. Próbáld újra.

seo_sign_in_error_title.comment: Heading (h1) shown on a full-screen error page when an OAuth sign-in attempt fails (e.g. user cancelled at Google, blocked third-party cookies, provider misconfiguration). Also used as the browser tab title. Keep it short — it's a heading. Apostrophe is a real curly/straight apostrophe in source; match whatever your locale uses for contractions. Should read as a calm statement, not an alarmist exclamation.

seo_sign_in_error_try_again.comment: Label on the primary action button below the error message. Clicking it reopens the sign-in dialog so the user can pick a provider again. Imperative verb, single short phrase. Avoid translating as a noun.

seo_sign_in_to_fotmob_predict.comment: Title for the sign in dialogue in the predictor game. Don't translate "FotMob Predict".

seo_sign_in_to_play.comment: Text for the button that opens the sign in dialogue in the predictor game.

seo_xg_table_explanation.comment: Text for explaining what the xG table is. The text has newline seperators in it.
seo_xg_table_explanation.english:
The xG table ranks teams based on their expected goals (xG) stats.

• Green numbers mean a team is doing better than expected.
• Red numbers mean a team is doing worse than expected.
• The small number next to the xG value shows the difference between expected and actual performance.

For more details on how it’s calculated, check the FAQ.
seo_xg_table_explanation.value:
Az xG-tabella a várható gólok (xG) alapján rangsorolja a csapatokat.

• A zöld számok azt jelentik, hogy a csapat a vártnál jobban teljesít.
• A piros számok azt jelentik, hogy a csapat a vártnál gyengébben teljesít.
• Az xG-érték melletti kis szám a várható és a tényleges teljesítmény különbségét mutatja.

A számítás részleteiről a GYIK-ban olvashatsz.

seo_xpts_explanation.comment: Explanation of the xG table. The text has newline separators in it.
seo_xpts_explanation.english:
Expected Points (xPts) reflect the number of points a team was expected to earn from a match, based on the quality of their chances measured by Expected Goals (xG).

xPts for a match are calculated by simulating possible outcomes using the quality of shots, expressed as xG. The simulation awards points for wins, draws, or losses based on xG.

The xPts are accumulated over the season to form the 'xG-table', also known as the 'Justice table', which provides an alternative view of team performance beyond actual points earned.
seo_xpts_explanation.value:
A várható pontok (xPts) azt mutatják, hány pontot kellett volna szereznie egy csapatnak egy meccsen a helyzetei minősége alapján, amelyet a várható gólok (xG) mérnek.

Egy meccs xPts-értékét a lehetséges kimenetelek szimulálásával számítjuk ki a lövések xG-ben kifejezett minősége alapján. A szimuláció az xG alapján ad pontot a győzelemért, a döntetlenért vagy a vereségért.

Az xPts-értékek az idény során összeadódnak, és így áll össze az „xG-tabella”, más néven „igazságtabella”, amely a ténylegesen megszerzett pontokon túl más nézőpontból mutatja a csapatok teljesítményét.

seo_xpts_explanation_green_numbers.english: Green numbers indicate better underlying numbers than a team's actual results.
seo_xpts_explanation_green_numbers.value: A zöld számok azt jelzik, hogy a mögöttes mutatók jobbak a csapat tényleges eredményeinél.

seo_xpts_explanation_red_numbers.comment: Explanation of the red numbers in the xG table. Underlying numbers refer to xG.

seo_xpts_explanation_red_numbers.value: A piros számok azt jelzik, hogy a mögöttes mutatók rosszabbak a csapat tényleges eredményeinél.
